_comment: Per-tracker overrides. TorrentLeech clears a hit-and-run at 240 h of seeding, but it counts
only the hours it actually saw: qBittorrent's own counter keeps running while announces fail,
and it ran for days with an invalid passkey after the account was disabled on 2026-08-16.
Measured on 2026-08-21, the client was ahead of the tracker by 26 to 118 hours across the 14
torrents on the H&R list, and Pokemon Detective Pikachu was 3 hours from being deleted at 237 h
of local time while the tracker had credited 152. Deleting it there would have left the warning
uncleared forever, which is the one outcome this script exists to prevent. 360 h covers the
worst measured gap with margin, and the ratio target is above 1.0 for the same reason.
_comment_digitalcore: DigitalCore clears a hit and run at 5 days of seeding or ratio 1:1, and its FAQ is explicit
that the site counts only the hours it saw announced, so the client's own counter is not
evidence. 168 h is a week: 40% above their 120 h, which covers announce gaps without holding
the disk for the ten days the generic private default was costing.
_comment_retrotoon: retrotoon asks for 72 h per torrent, reached inside the first 10 days, and calls it its
strictest rule. 96 h is a third more than that, which covers a lagging tracker clock while
still freeing the disk two and a half times sooner than the generic 240 h default did.
_comment_quiet: `quiet` is where each tracker's economics live. The site's own hit and run rule decides when a
torrent MAY go; its upload rate decides whether it SHOULD. Measured 2026-08-22: torrents seeded
40 to 157 h had uploaded 0.00 GB while ones a few hours old were doing 0.13 to 0.82 GB/h, so a
goal of 'ratio 1.2' was deleting the best earner in the client and keeping the worst.
min_upload_gb_per_day is the floor below which a torrent is not paying for its disk any more.

_comment: Their H&R system is disabled site-wide right now and documented as returning at
72 h. Kept at their documented number so nothing changes when it comes back.
